questions.question: A homogeneous linear ODE with constant real coefficients has characteristic polynomial $p(r)=(r+1)^3$, so its solutions are $(c_1+c_2t+c_3t^2)\mathrm{e}^{-t}$. Is the equation asymptotically stable (every solution of the homogeneous equation tends to $0$ as $t\to\infty$)?
options: No, since a repeated root always makes it unstable
No, since the term $c_3t^2\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ is unbounded
Yes, since $t^j\mathrm{e}^{-t}\to0$ for every power $j$
Only if $c_2=c_3=0$, leaving the pure $\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ term

questions.question: For constant-coefficient $x^{(n)}+\dots+a_1x'+a_0x=c$ with constant $c$, every solution tends to $c/a_0$ if and only if all characteristic roots have negative real part. Why is $a_0\neq0$ assumed?
options: With $a_0=0$ the equation is no longer linear
With $a_0=0$ all roots are forced to be positive
$c/a_0$ needs $a_0\neq0$; if $a_0=0$ then $0$ is a root
With $a_0=0$ every solution is a constant function

questions.question: For $x''+3x'+2x=g(t)$ with a given forcing $g$ and a particular solution $x_p$, does the choice of $g$ affect whether every solution satisfies $x(t)-x_p(t)\to0$ as $t\to\infty$?
options: No: this depends only on the roots of $r^2+3r+2$
Yes: it holds only when $g$ is bounded
Yes: it holds only when $g$ is a constant
No: it holds for every equation once $g\not\equiv0$

questions.question: Consider $x''+a_1x'+a_0x=0$ with real constants $a_1$ and $a_0<0$. Using that the characteristic roots have sum $-a_1$ and product $a_0$, what can be concluded?
options: It is asymptotically stable whenever $a_1$ is large
It is bounded but not asymptotically stable
The roots are complex, so stability depends on $a_1$
One root is positive, so it is unstable for every $a_1$

questions.question: Is $x''+6x'+13x=0$ asymptotically stable (every solution of the homogeneous equation tends to $0$ as $t\to\infty$)?
options: No: complex roots make the solutions oscillate
Yes: the roots $-3\pm2i$ have real part $-3$
No: the imaginary parts $\pm2$ are not negative
No: it is stable, but not asymptotically

questions.question: Every solution of $x''+5x'+4x=8$ has a limit as $t\to\infty$. What is it?
For which values of the real parameter $k$ is $x''+kx'+3x=0$ asymptotically stable (every solution of the homogeneous equation tends to $0$ as $t\to\infty$)?
options: Exactly for $k>0$
Exactly for $k\geq0$
Exactly for $k>2\sqrt{3}$
Exactly for $k<0$

questions.question: Four homogeneous constant-coefficient linear ODEs (continuous time) have the characteristic roots listed. Which one is asymptotically stable (every solution of the homogeneous equation tends to $0$ as $t\to\infty$)?
options: Roots $-3$ and $0.2$
Roots $-1$ and $\pm2i$
Roots $0.3\pm0.4i$
Roots $-0.5\pm4i$

questions.question: The equation $x''=0$ has characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^2$ and solutions $c_1+c_2t$. How is it classified on $[0,\infty)$?
options: Asymptotically stable: no root is positive
Unstable: some solutions are unbounded
Stable: all roots have real part $0$
Stable: the constant solutions do not move

questions.question: For $x''+a_1x'+a_0x=c$ with constants $a_0\neq0$ and $c$, the constant $x_p=c/a_0$ is always a solution. When does every solution tend to $c/a_0$ as $t\to\infty$?
options: Always, since $c/a_0$ is an equilibrium of the equation
Exactly when $c$ and $a_0$ have the same sign, so $c/a_0>0$
Exactly when both roots of $r^2+a_1r+a_0$ have negative real part
Exactly when both roots of $r^2+a_1r+a_0$ are real and distinct

questions.question: The homogeneous equation $x''''+2x''+x=0$ has characteristic polynomial $(r^2+1)^2$, so all roots $\pm i$ have real part $0$. Why are some solutions unbounded on $[0,\infty)$?
options: Real part $0$ always makes solutions unbounded
A fourth-order equation needs four negative roots
The coefficient of $x'''$ is zero, so it is unstable
The repeated pair gives terms such as $t\cos t$

questions.question: Equation (I) $x''+2x'+101x=0$ has roots $-1\pm10i$; equation (II) $x''+4x'+5x=0$ has roots $-2\pm i$. Whose solutions have the faster-decaying amplitude envelope?
options: (I), since its frequency $10$ is larger
(I), since its coefficient $101$ is larger
Neither: both envelopes decay at one rate
(II), since its envelope is $\mathrm{e}^{-2t}$

questions.question: The homogeneous equation $x'''+3x''+4x'+2x=0$ has characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^3+3r^2+4r+2$, and $p(-1)=0$. How is the equation classified on $[0,\infty)$?
options: Stable, not asymptotically: the other roots are $\pm i$
Unstable: the other roots $1\pm i$ have positive real part
Asymptotically stable: the other roots are $-1\pm i$
Undecided: positive coefficients do not suffice for $n\geq3$

questions.question: With $y_1=x$, $y_2=x'$ an equation $x''+a_1x'+a_0x=0$ becomes $\boldsymbol{y}'=M\boldsymbol{y}$ with $M=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-5&-2\end{pmatrix}$. What are the eigenvalues of $M$, and is the equation asymptotically stable (every solution of the homogeneous equation tends to $0$ as $t\to\infty$)?
options: $-1\pm2i$; asymptotically stable
$0$ and $-2$; not asymptotically stable
$1\pm2i$; unstable
$\pm\sqrt{5}\,i$; stable, not asymptotically

questions.question: The equation $x''+3x'+2x=g(t)$ has characteristic roots $-1,-2$. For the forcing $g(t)=2t$ one particular solution is $x_p=t-\tfrac{3}{2}$. What do all solutions do as $t\to\infty$?
options: $x(t)-x_p(t)\to0$, while $x(t)$ itself grows like $t$
$x(t)\to0$, since the equation is asymptotically stable
$x(t)$ is bounded, since the equation is asymptotically stable
$x(t)-x_p(t)$ is unbounded, since the forcing $2t$ is unbounded

questions.question: Sampling the mode $\mathrm{e}^{rt}$ of a differential equation at integer times $t$ gives $\lambda^t$ with $\lambda=\mathrm{e}^{r}$. For $r=\alpha+i\beta$, which condition on $\lambda$ corresponds to the continuous-time condition $\alpha<0$?
options: $\operatorname{Re}\lambda<0$
$|\lambda|<1$
$\lambda<1$ as a real number
$|\lambda|>1$

questions.question: The equation $x''-x'-2x=4$ has characteristic roots $2$ and $-1$ and equilibrium $x_p=-2$, so $x=-2+c_1\mathrm{e}^{2t}+c_2\mathrm{e}^{-t}$. Which initial data $\big(x(0),x'(0)\big)$ give a solution with $x(t)\to-2$?

A homogeneous constant-coefficient linear ODE has a simple pair of characteristic roots $\pm\mathrm{i}\beta$ with $\beta\neq0$, and at least one further root; every remaining root has strictly negative real part. What do the solutions do on $[0,\infty)$?
options: All tend to $0$ as $t\to\infty$
All are bounded, but some do not tend to $0$
Some grow without bound, like $t\cos\beta t$
All are periodic with period $2\pi/\beta$

questions.question: Let $p(r)=r^n+a_{n-1}r^{n-1}+\dots+a_1r+a_0$ have real coefficients and $n\geq3$. How are "all $a_i>0$" and "all roots have negative real part" related?
options: Positive coefficients are necessary but not sufficient
Positive coefficients guarantee it but are not required
The two conditions are equivalent for every $n$
Positive coefficients are neither necessary nor sufficient

questions.question: Classify the equation $x''+2x'=0$ on $[0,\infty)$; its characteristic roots are $0$ and $-2$.
options: Asymptotically stable, since $a_1=2>0$
Stable, but not asymptotically stable
Unstable, since the root $0$ gives growth
Unstable, since $a_0=0$ is not positive
